title: WPSS/1158/2011 of SMT PRITI RANI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1158 of 2011
Smt. Priti Rani Ö Petitioner
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Mr. S.K. Mandal, Advocate, present for the petitioner
Mr. Subhash Upadhyay, Standing Counsel, present for the State of Uttarakhand
Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Advocate, present for respondent No. 3.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
 1. Heard Mr. S.K. Mandal, learned counsel for
the petitioner, Mr. Subhash Upadhyay, learned Standing
Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand, Mr. Rakesh
Thapliyal, learned counsel for respondent No. 3 and
perused the record.
2. The petitioner was a candidate for the post of
Assistant Teacher in L.T. Grade (Arts) i.e. ìKALAî. She
has not been selected in the examination. The grievance
of the petitioner is that the quota points which was liable
to be given to her for B.Ed. qualification have not been
added in the total score as a consequence of which she
has been deprived of for the selection. It has further
pleaded that she is B.Ed. with very high percent of marks
and had these marks been added in the total number of
marks, she would liable to be selected.
3. The reason given in the counter affidavit by the
State is that as per the Rules known as ìUttarakhand
Subordinate Education (Trained Graduates Grade) Service
Rules, 2006, there is no provision for giving additional
quality points for the marks of B.Ed. degree to the
candidates. The qualification for an Assistant Teacher

2
(Arts) reads as under:-
ì5 Assistant Master/Assistant Mistress (Arts)
1. B.F.A. degree or a bachelorís degree with Art
subject from a University established by law in
India.
2. Fine Arts Diploma of the Government School
of Arts and Crafts, Lucknow.
 Or
Bachelorís degree in Arts with Drawing and
Painting from a University established by law in
India.
 Or
Fine Art Diploma of Kala Bhawan,
Shantiniketan.
 Or
Final Drawing Teachership Examination
Calcutta.î
4. The same qualification is also given in the
advertisement published for the said post. From the
perusal of the Rules (mentioned above) as well as the
advertisement it shows that B.Ed. is not a qualification
for the post of Assistant Teacher (Arts) since it was not a
required qualification. Even though the petitioner is
B.Ed., such quota marks were not liable to be given to
her, as she is a candidate for an Assistant Teacher (Arts)
for which B.Ed. is not a qualification.
5. The writ petition is totally misconceived and is
hereby dismissed. No order as to costs.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
09.09.2013
Aswal
